proposals.evidence: Turner explicitly lists Gawri šūnā and Marathi suṇẽ under the first śuna branch, contrasting the feminine śunī and aspirated śunakha branches. Gawri śūna and the western Bhil masculine hūṇo forms fit that whole stem, with the western s-to-h correspondence retained. Feminine-looking huṇi and Kullu śoṇ are left unassigned because subsection choice is less secure.

proposals.evidence: Turner’s onomatopoeic kukkuṭa family explicitly includes Bashkarik kukur/kikir, Maiya koko, Shina koko/kukūĩ, Oriya kukuṛā, Gujarati kukṛɔ/kukṛī, and Nepali kukhro with expressive aspiration; the addendum gives Kullu-area kukhṛɔ/kukhṛī. These whole male/female or single-stem survey responses fit that documented family. Both members of each included slash response are accounted for; unrelated kakavãk and murga responses are excluded.
